Briefing Diario

Miércoles 28 de octubre de 2026  ·  939 palabras  ·  5 min de lectura

Reinsurance News abre la jornada recordando que el riesgo catastrófico sigue siendo el gran acelerador del cambio en el sector reasegurador. No es la única señal del día: Morocco también mueve ficha en la misma dirección. De los 118 artículos rastreados hoy, 40 han activado nuestras alertas de señal — una densidad de noticias relevante que no veíamos en días. A continuación, las cinco historias que hemos seleccionado entre 118 artículos de más de 40 fuentes, ordenadas por impacto real sobre el negocio asegurador.

1. 🌪️ Clima & Catástrofes

EU unveils climate resilience framework with re/insurance protection gap in focus

The European Commission has presented an EU Framework for Climate Resilience to strengthen Europe’s ability to anticipate, prepare for and manage climate risks, highlighting re/insurance as a “crucial element” in this equation. The framework reportedly aims to embed climate resilience across EU policies, support local and regional authorities, and encourage private-sector investment in adaptation, with an estimated €70 billion a year needed to adapt Europe’s infrastructure and economy. We are ensuring that climate resilience will be included in policies across the continent, supporting investment, innovation and long-term growth.” Alongside the framework, the Commission has proposed a Climate Resilience Law to establish common assumptions for future global warming, simplify national planning through a single strategic plan for each member state, and improve the consistency of climate risk assessments.

  1. El dato clave: The framework reportedly aims to embed climate resilience across EU policies, support local and regional authorities, and encourage private-sector investment in adaptation, with an estimated €70 billion a year needed to adapt Europe’s infrastructure and economy.
  2. ¿Por qué importa? Impacto directo en exposición, pricing y reservas del sector.
  3. ¿Qué vigilar? El sector deberá revisar modelos de pricing y cobertura en las zonas afectadas ante el incremento de eventos extremos.

2. 🌪️ Clima & Catástrofes

Morocco targets regulatory framework for insurance securitization, including cat bonds

The government of Morocco is now aiming to prepare a regulatory framework to allow for the securitization of insurance risks, including through catastrophe bonds, as the country seemingly aims to support issuance as well as to be a beneficiary of risk transfer to the capital markets. The new Finance Bill for fiscal year 2027 calls for the preparation of a regulatory framework for the securitization of insurance risks, including catastrophe bonds. It’s particularly notable to see the mention of Morocco having a goal to construct its own regulatory framework for the securitization of insurance risks, as a way to bring third-party capital more directly into the country to support natural disaster, catastrophe and climate risk transfer.

  1. El dato clave: The new Finance Bill for fiscal year 2027 calls for the preparation of a regulatory framework for the securitization of insurance risks, including catastrophe bonds.
  2. ¿Por qué importa? The new Finance Bill for fiscal year 2027 calls for the preparation of a regulatory framework for the securitization of insurance risks, including catastrophe bonds.
  3. ¿Qué vigilar? El sector deberá revisar modelos de pricing y cobertura en las zonas afectadas ante el incremento de eventos extremos.

3. 💰 Inversión

Mapfre Re’s 9M’26 profit climbs 11.8% to €286m

Mapfre Re, Mapfre’s Reinsurance and Global Risks arm, grew profit 11.8% to €286 million in the first nine months of 2026, helped by a 67.8% rise in its Non-Life financial result, even as its combined ratio worsened and it absorbed the impact of the earthquake in Colombia. At group level, Mapfre’s net profit for the first nine months of 2026 rose 11.5% to €924 million, while total premiums grew 2% to €22.8 billion, with Life up 5% and Non-Life up 1.1%. Mapfre Re’s premiums were broadly steady at €6.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026, with Mapfre citing declining reinsurance and insurance rates.

  1. El dato clave: Mapfre Re’s 9M’26 profit climbs 11.8% to €286m.
  2. ¿Por qué importa? Nueva financiación que puede acelerar la competencia en el sector.
  3. ¿Qué vigilar? El capital invertido anticipa las áreas donde los incumbentes afrontarán mayor presión competitiva en los próximos 12-24 meses.

Fla. Reforms Cut Property Premiums but Data Show Multifamily Liability Rates Up

Data from Advocate Technologies, a data analytics firm that tracks commercial and commercial residential rates around the country for the insurance industry, show that property insurance premiums for multifamily dwellings in Florida, like those for most other properties, have indeed fallen sharply in the last two years. In other words, it seems that Florida’s historic 2022 and 2023 legislative reforms have had a significant impact on property insurance by disincentivizing excessive claims litigation, but liability claims and lawsuits continue to cost insurers and insureds, at least in the multifamily segment, the Advocate data and reports suggest. The data for more than 1,000 Florida properties show that for Florida multifamily property insurance for all categories of structures and coverage, except condominiums, with primary and excess coverage included, the median premium per door has dropped from an early 2025 number of $797—almost double the rate in other Southeastern states—to $472 in April of this year.
